title: Case report for case number 2602410200 — the case number SMPD cited in ALPR searches
summary:
A one-item request to the records custodian, not the ALPR program:

- Item 1: any incident, crime, or case report bearing case number 2602410200.

A copy redacted as the Department deems necessary is acceptable, and the request asks the Department to state in writing if no record bearing that case number exists. If the record is withheld in whole or in part, it asks for the exemption relied upon and the basis on which no reasonably segregable portion could be released under Gov. Code § 7922.525(b).

On 2026-08-28 the Department invoked its Gov. Code § 7922.530(a) duty to assist and asked the requester to confirm the incident number "to avoid any possible typos," warning that no reply within 30 days would be treated as withdrawal. The requester confirmed the number the same morning and stated it is not a transcription error.

policy_promises.quote: records of investigations conducted by, or investigatory files compiled by, any state or local police agency
policy_promises.tests: Whether a case number the Department has entered as its justification for ALPR searches, and treated as investigative, corresponds to any investigation at all.

policy_promises.quote: agency must notify requester within 10 calendar days whether it will produce records
policy_promises.tests: Whether the Department issues a written determination on a single named case number, including a written statement if no such record exists.

policy_promises.policy: Gov. Code § 7922.530(a) / Rogers v. Superior Court (1993) 19 Cal.App.4th 469, 481
policy_promises.quote: duty to assist the member of the public in making a focused and effective request
policy_promises.tests: Whether the clarification round-trip resolves to a substantive answer or restarts the response clock on an unambiguous, already-confirmed identifier.

prior_pra_refs.note: Denied in full 2026-07-29 on the theory that ALPR audit entries document "the category of criminal offense under investigation and the time frame of the search." This request tests that premise against one such entry's own case number.
Narrowed refile of W013113, denied in full 2026-08-04 on the same rationale, adding Civ. Code § 1798.90.55(b) and Gov. Code § 7927.705.
The Department's own rolling search-audit production, which shows the reason field as "Category - detail" with the detail generally a case number.

filed_because: San Mateo PD ran four ALPR searches on 2026-02-15 (04:46-04:59 UTC, 634 networks each) citing the reason "Larceny/Theft Offenses - 2602410200." San Mateo CAD numbers encode YYMMDD plus a per-day sequence, and 2602410200 decodes to February 41, 2026 — a date that does not exist. The searches are visible because Los Altos PD produced its Flock network audit in full, including the searching organization and reason, under its own PRA 26-366; San Mateo PD has withheld the same field on its own network-audit entries as investigative. Asking the records custodian for the underlying report puts that theory to the test: if the answer is that no record bearing this case number exists, then a value the Department redacts as investigative refers to no investigation, and the categorical § 7923.600 premise fails on its own facts. Routed to the records custodian rather than the ALPR program, so it is a separate matter from the audit-log requests and unlikely to be consolidated with them.
notes:
Filed 2026-08-24 11:43 PM; auto-acknowledged the same minute. Statutory determination due 2026-09-03.

2026-08-28 7:10 AM: Senior Records Specialist Jodi Ferreira requested clarification under Gov. Code § 7922.530(a) confirming the incident number, with a 30-day non-response-is-withdrawal warning. Confirmed by the requester at 9:26 AM the same day.

One of sixteen impossible-date case numbers in the sweep of SMPD-cited numbers across partner productions; chosen because it is the most recent (current reason-field regime) and is cited by San Mateo PD itself, so a "no responsive records" answer cannot be deflected to another agency. Not among the rows edited in the W012541 audit PDFs — this attacks the exemption, not the alteration.
